correctness.rationale: The discriminant follows from evaluation of the polar radical. The primitive linear polynomial is geometrically irreducible and the singular plane has codimension two, giving normality. The graph blowup has strict transform P_B(K), smooth by surjectivity of D²,E²,F²; ambient adjunction gives discrepancy zero. A global section of the affine torsor would split the bundle extension, whose class is nonzero because DEF is the unique degree-three monomial absent from the image of the twisted Frobenius–Euler map. Scissor and affine-torsor local triviality yield the motivic and field-count formulas. All computations were run from included code and do not replace these geometric proofs.

value.rationale: A classical universal singularity gains an explicit crepant smooth model and a nonvanishing obstruction to global affine-bundle triviality, while its seemingly trivial motivic class and exact point counts contrast with the nonsplit torsor. Both the local-to-global extension and motivic consequences are structural, naturally motivated algebraic-geometric facts.
